global.title: Global settings
global.description: Process-wide HAProxy settings: user and group, logging, connection limit, admin socket and default TLS.

defaults.title: Defaults
defaults.description: Anything you put here is inherited by the frontend, backend and listen sections that follow (until the next defaults).

frontend.title: Traffic entry point
frontend.description: Where HAProxy listens (bind) and which rules decide the backend each request goes to.

backend.title: Server pool
backend.description: The destination servers, how load is spread across them and how their health is checked.

listen.title: Entry point + servers
listen.description: Frontend and backend in a single section. Typical for TCP services or the statistics page.

resolvers.title: DNS resolution
resolvers.description: DNS servers HAProxy queries to resolve server names at runtime.

peers.title: Replicas (peers)
peers.description: Other HAProxy instances to synchronize stick-tables with (persistence, rate limits).

userlist.title: Users
userlist.description: Users and groups for HTTP basic authentication.

mailers.title: Email alerts
mailers.description: SMTP servers used to send notifications about server state changes.

cache.title: HTTP cache
cache.description: In-memory cache for small, frequently requested HTTP responses.

http-errors.title: Error pages
http-errors.description: Reusable set of custom error pages.

ring.title: Log buffer
ring.description: In-memory circular buffer for logs or traces.

program.title: External program
program.description: External process started and supervised by the HAProxy master.

directives.daemon: Runs HAProxy in the background (as a daemon).
directives.master-worker: Master-worker mode: a master process supervises the workers and allows zero-downtime reloads.
directives.uid: Numeric UID the process runs as.
directives.gid: Numeric GID the process runs as.
directives.chroot: Confines the process to a directory (chroot) to limit the damage of a break-in:
directives.pidfile: File the PID is written to:
directives.cpu-map: Pins threads to specific CPU cores:
directives.ca-base: Base directory for relative CA file paths:
directives.crt-base: Base directory for relative certificate paths:
directives.ssl-default-bind-ciphers: Ciphers for TLS ≤ 1.2 on all binds with ssl.
directives.ssl-default-bind-ciphersuites: Cipher suites for TLS 1.3 on all binds with ssl.
directives.ssl-default-server-ciphersuites: Cipher suites for TLS 1.3 towards servers.
directives.ssl-server-verify: Whether server certificates are verified by default:
directives.lua-load: Loads a Lua script at startup:
directives.lua-prepend-path: Adds a search path for Lua modules:
directives.presetenv: Sets an environment variable if it is not already set:
directives.server-state-file: File where server state is saved across reloads:
directives.server-state-base: Base directory for the state files:
directives.insecure-fork-wanted: Allows creating child processes (external checks, Lua). Weakens security.
directives.localpeer: Name of this instance within the peers section:
directives.log-send-hostname: Includes the hostname in syslog messages.
directives.h1-case-adjust: Adjusts the letter case of a specific HTTP/1 header:
directives.hash-balance-factor: Relative load limit with consistent hashing:
directives.dispatch: Sends all traffic to a single address (legacy mode):
directives.fullconn: Connection count at which servers reach their dynamic maxconn:
directives.retry-on: Cases in which the request is retried on another server (layer 7 retries):
directives.log-format: Custom format for each log line.
directives.log-format-sd: Structured data (RFC 5424) for each log line.
directives.unique-id-format: Format of each request's unique identifier:
directives.unique-id-header: Header used to send the unique identifier to the server:
directives.errorfiles: Uses the error pages of an http-errors section:
directives.errorloc: Redirects to another URL instead of showing an error page:
directives.errorloc302: Redirects (302) to another URL instead of showing an error page:
directives.errorloc303: Redirects (303) to another URL instead of showing an error page:
directives.monitor-uri: Path that always answers 200 (for external load balancer probes):
directives.monitor: Condition that makes monitor-uri answer with a failure:
directives.source: Source IP used to connect to servers:
directives.email-alert: Email alerts when server state changes:
directives.load-server-state-from-file: Loads the saved server state on reload:
directives.grace: Grace period before no longer accepting connections when stopping:
directives.http-send-name-header: Sends the server a header with the name of the chosen server:
directives.max-keep-alive-queue: Maximum queue length to reuse keep-alive connections:
directives.resolve_retries: Retries of each DNS query before giving up:
directives.process-vary: Takes the Vary header into account when caching:

options.httplog: Detailed **HTTP logs** (method, path, status code, timings)
options.dontlognull: Does not log connections that send no data (probes, scanners)
options.forwardfor: Adds the **X-Forwarded-For** header with the client's real IP
options.http-server-close: Closes the server connection after each response (keeps keep-alive with the client)
options.httpclose: Closes the connection after each request
options.redispatch: If the server picked by persistence is down, resends the request to another one
options.ssl-hello-chk: Health checks using an SSLv3 hello
options.abortonclose: Cancels queued requests if the client goes away
options.allbackups: Uses all backup servers at once
options.http-buffer-request: Waits for the request body before choosing the backend
options.logasap: Logs the request without waiting for it to finish
options.log-separate-errors: Logs errors with a higher severity
options.persist: Keeps persistence even if the server goes down
options.prefer-last-server: Tries to reuse the last server used
options.disable-h2-upgrade: Does not allow upgrading to cleartext HTTP/2
options.h1-case-adjust-bogus-client: Adjusts header letter case for legacy clients
options.h1-case-adjust-bogus-server: Adjusts header letter case for legacy servers
options.external-check: Health checks using an external command
options.transparent: Connects to the original destination IP

timeouts.connect: to establish the TCP connection to a server
timeouts.server: waiting for data from the server
timeouts.http-request: to receive the complete HTTP request (protects against slowloris)
timeouts.http-keep-alive: waiting for the next request on a keep-alive connection
timeouts.queue: a request can wait in the queue
timeouts.check: extra to complete a health check
timeouts.tarpit: a request is held in the tarpit

balance.leastconn: picks the server with the **fewest active connections** (ideal for long sessions)
balance.first: fills the first server up to its maxconn before moving on to the next
balance.source: **hash of the client IP**: the same client always goes to the same server

fetches.ssl_c_verify: the result of verifying the client certificate
fetches.src_conn_cur: the number of open connections from that IP
fetches.sc0_conn_cur: the client's number of open connections
